issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe lectureName as a String, but the solution implementation declares lectureName as a LectureName object. This attribute type mismatch creates confusion about the expected type and prevents students from directly following the UML or using simple String-based getters/setters as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent across artifacts. Prefer changing the solution to use a String for lectureName (and remove or repurpose LectureName class), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and document a LectureName type. The simplest fix: use String lectureName in the solution's field, constructor, getters and setters to match the UML and exercise text.

issues.description: The constructor in the solution accepts a LectureName parameter for lectureName, while the exercise and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String and require a constructor initializing all attributes in the UML order. This constructor parameter type mismatch will prevent students from instantiating Lecture objects as described and conflicts with the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature with the UML and problem description. Change the solution constructor to accept a String lectureName as the first parameter (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors), or update the problem statement/template to clearly require a LectureName object and demonstrate how students should construct one.

issues.description: The solution's getter and setter for lectureName are inconsistent with the declared field type. The problem and UML expect a String-based getter/setter, but the solution declares getLectureName() returning String while returning a LectureName field, and setLectureName(String) assigning a String to a LectureName field. This creates compile errors and confuses students about the correct method signatures and types to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure getter and setter types match the field type. If lectureName is intended to be a String (as per the problem), change the field to String and keep getLectureName(): String and setLectureName(String). If using a LectureName type is desired, change the getter to return LectureName and the setter to accept LectureName, and update the problem statement and template to reflect this type change.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String, and the template expects a simple lectureName attribute to be implemented accordingly. The solution repository, however, introduces a separate LectureName class and declares the lectureName field as type LectureName. This changes the expected type/name abstraction for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and creates mapping confusion for students who expect a String field and String-based getters/setters per the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the lecture name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field (private String lectureName) and adjust constructor, getters and setters accordingly so it matches the UML and template, or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and document the LectureName class as the required type for lectureName. Preferred: use option (A) to align solution with the original UML (String) and reduce extraneous cognitive load.
